units.text: INT. CORNER LAUNDROMAT - NIGHT
A long fluorescent room that hums on a note slightly flat of pleasant.
Forty-year-old dryers turn their round windows to the room like patient, soapy eyes.
Linoleum the color of weak tea.
A vending machine sells one kind of detergent and one kind of regret.
At the far end, a wall intercom, brown with age, crackles every so often like a throat clearing itself.
THEODORA "TEDDY" MAKINDE-LOWE (60s, silver hair pinned under a scarf, the posture of a retired headmistress) folds towels with military corners.
She does it slowly.
She does it as an argument.
At the next folding table, GUILLERMINA "MINA" ASHWORTH-REYES (60s, jewelry that clinks, a laugh kept in reserve) is unloading a basket of what appear to be fifty identical white shirts.
Neither woman looks at the other.
The dryers turn.
They've changed the soap.
units.name: MINA

units.text: They have not.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: It smells different.
units.name: MINA

units.text: You smell different. You've changed your perfume.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: I have not.
units.name: MINA

units.text: It has a note of disappointment in it.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: Mina sets down a shirt, very gently, as one sets down a grenade.
She smooths it.
She picks up another.
Is that a towel or a tribute?
units.name: MINA

units.text: It is a towel folded the way a towel is meant to be folded.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: It's a bit sharp for a towel. She'd never fold them like that, you know.
units.name: MINA

units.text: She would not. She didn't have the discipline. She had charm, which is the next best thing to a fully ironed shirt.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: Mina's hands go still on the shirt in front of her.
Don't.
units.name: MINA

units.text: I merely said...
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: Don't do the voice. Don't do the voice you do.
units.name: MINA

units.text: What voice? This is my voice. It has been my voice since nineteen-sixty-one.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: The wall intercom CRACKLES.
Both women look up.
Attention customers. Dryer six is finished. Dryer six is finished. Please remove your items from dryer six.
units.name: ATTENDANT

units.text: Neither moves.
Dryer six, at the end of the row, gives a long, low buzz.
That's yours.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: Yours.
units.name: MINA

units.text: You were by it.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: You were nearer.
units.name: MINA

units.text: Dryer six. Also, someone has left a casserole dish in dryer three.
units.name: ATTENDANT

units.text: Teddy goes pink at the ears.
Mina notices.
She smiles, slowly, like a woman who has just found the pearl in the oyster.
A casserole dish.
units.name: MINA

units.text: It's nothing.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: In a dryer.
units.name: MINA

units.text: It had gone cold, and I thought...
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: You thought you'd warm it up in a dryer. At a laundromat. At midnight.
units.name: MINA

units.text: I was having an evening.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: Mina starts to laugh.
It's a small laugh at first, a hiccup behind her teeth.
She presses a hand over her mouth.
The bracelets clink.
Stop that.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: I'm not doing anything.
units.name: MINA

units.text: You're laughing at me.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: I'm laughing at a casserole.
units.name: MINA

units.text: It was her recipe.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: The laughter stops as if a switch had been thrown.
The dryers keep turning.
The room hums its flat note.
Mina picks a shirt up, puts it down.
Teddy folds a towel, unfolds it, folds it again.
It was her recipe.
units.name: MINA

units.text: It's the only one I have.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: I have the chicken.
units.name: MINA

units.text: You have the chicken.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: I've had it for six years and I've never once made it.
units.name: MINA

units.text: Nor I the casserole. Until tonight. I put it in the dryer and I stood there and I watched it go round and I thought, this is the stupidest thing I have ever done.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: It is the stupidest thing.
units.name: MINA

units.text: It is.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: It's wonderful.
units.name: MINA

units.text: Mina, I cannot do this to a perfectly good evening.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: She bangs a folded towel down on the table.
A second.
A third.
She grabs the stack and hurls the whole thing across the room.
It hits the vending machine with a soft, ridiculous FLUMP.
Mina stares.
Then she picks up a shirt and throws it, too.
It lands on Teddy's head.
For a moment Teddy sits there under it, motionless, like a ghost in a bad school play.
That was hers.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: Was it?
units.name: MINA

units.text: It was a very nice shirt.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: She pulls it off.
Both women are laughing now, helplessly, hanging onto the folding table.
Customers. Please keep your grief to the back of the store.
units.name: ATTENDANT

units.text: That makes it worse.
They have to sit down on the floor.
